title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (v10)
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), high-level design specs, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family (internal codename: unified-inference). It is intended for engineering, product, go-to-market, and customer success stakeholders who need a single source-of-truth for the v10 release and near-term roadmap.

Goals and success metrics

- Primary goal: Provide a single, consistent developer experience that delivers predictable latency, lower unit costs, and frictionless portability across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.
- Success metrics (measurable):
  - Latency: p50 <= 20ms, p95 <= 120ms for single-stream generation workloads (short prompt, 50 tokens).
  - Availability: 99.95% regionally for Hosted; 99.9% for Dedicated SLA customers.
  - Cost: 15-30% reduction in $/1k tokens compared to v8 baseline for typical chat workloads via improved batching + KV caching.
  - Adoption: 20% increase in customers using multi-deployment routing (Hosted -> Dedicated fallback) within 6 months of launch.
  - Quality: No more than 1% uplift in hallucination/regression alerts across tracked prompt sets during canary.

Problem statement

Teams building on top of Redwood currently face trade-offs between cost, latency, and deployment constraints. Customers request: predictable economics when workloads scale, simpler migration between Hosted and Dedicated, and a single API surface that supports function/tool calling, streaming, and structured outputs without rework. The Unified Inference v10 roadmap focuses on reducing cognitive load for engineers while improving unit economics and regional resilience.

Scope

In scope (v10):
- Unified API: single REST/SDK contract that supports text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with a versioned model catalog.
- Model routing and cost-aware fallbacks: policy engine that routes by latency, cost, and region with automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Smart batching & KV cache improvements: adaptive batching heuristics and prefix/KV cache persistence per customer route.
- Pricing & packaging update: introduce Predictable-Throughput tier (reserved tokens/min) for Dedicated and bundled observability credits for Enterprise.
- Developer ergonomics: improved SDK defaults, streaming heuristics, and better error messages.

Out of scope (v10):
- Major compiler/runtime rewrites (deferred to runtime v3 in 2027).
- New on-prem hardware profiles beyond current certified list.

Requirements (PRD)

Priority: Must / Should / Nice-to-have

1) Core API compatibility (MUST)
- Maintain backward-compatible REST endpoints for generate, chat, embeddings, and rerank.
- Version the API: clients can specify api_version=2026-12-v1.
- Support streaming responses with resumable tokens for large payloads.

2) Model routing / fallback (MUST)
- Policy config per customer route: primary_model, fallback_models (ordered), routing_policy (latency|cost|region_priority).
- Automatic fallback trigger: if p95 latency > configured threshold OR error_rate > threshold OR capacity_unavailable.

3) Batching & KV cache (MUST)
- Adaptive batcher that adjusts batch size based on observed latency SLOs and sequence-length distribution.
- Persistent KV cache keyed by route + model + prompt-prefix hash with TTL default 12h; configurable per-customer.

4) Pricing and packaging (SHOULD)
- Introduce Predictable-Throughput tier for Dedicated with reserved tokens/min and burst buffer.
- Bundle 30 days of enhanced observability (full trace retention) with Enterprise Dedicated contracts.
- Publish publicly the unit economics table and a cost-savings estimator in the docs portal.

5) Telemetry and quality guardrails (MUST)
- Route-level metrics: token_count, latency_p50/p95/p99, error_rate, cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution.
- Automatic regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets (configurable per route).

6) Security & compliance (MUST for Private)
- KMS integrations for Private deployments; audit logging enabled by default; RBAC for route-level controls.

Design & Architecture (high-level)

The v10 product design emphasizes layering: API surface -> routing & policy -> serving runtime -> infra & storage. Key components described below.

- API Gateway: Accepts requests, enforces quotas, authentication, and delegates to Policy Engine.
- Policy Engine: Evaluates routing policy, chooses target (Hosted cluster / Dedicated pool / Private endpoint), and constructs execution plan (batching constraints, cache hints).
- Batcher + Cache Layer: Continuous batching engine with per-route adaptive parameters and a distributed KV cache (in-memory shard + durable backing for cache persistence).

- Serving Runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine capable of quantized model execution, KV cache retrieval, and streaming token emission.
- Observability & Tracing: Per-token traces sampled at 0.1% by default, enriched with model variant and batch metadata.

Architecture diagram (textual)

[API Gateway] -> [Policy Engine] -> {choose: Hosted / Dedicated / Private} -> [Batcher + KV Cache] -> [Serving Runtime (GPU)] -> [Response Streamer]

API contract examples

1) Generate (JSON example)

Request:
{
  "model": "rwd-3-small",
  "input": "Summarize the following user message...",
  "max_tokens": 128,
  "stream": true,
  "route_id": "customer-123/main-chat",
  "api_version": "2026-12-v1"
}

Response (streaming frames):
- data: {"token": "Hello", "logprob": -0.02}
- data: {"token": "world", "logprob": -0.01}

2) Route config (YAML example)

route_id: customer-123/main-chat
primary_model: rwd-3-small
fallback_models:
  - rwd-3-medium-quant
routing_policy: "latency"
latency_threshold_ms: 200
cache_ttl: 12h

SLOs and thresholds (table)

| Metric | Target (Hosted) | Target (Dedicated SLA) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Latency p50 (50-token) | <= 20ms | <= 18ms | Measured at edge after streaming setup |
| Latency p95 (50-token) | <= 120ms | <= 90ms | Policy override allowed per route |
| Availability | 99.95% | 99.90% | Regionally measured |
| Cache hit rate | >= 30% (target) | >= 40% | Dependent on workload repetition |
| Error rate (5xx) | < 0.1% | < 0.05% | SRE alerting threshold |

Pricing & Packaging notes

Pricing goals: be transparent, provide options for predictable spend, and align incentives to efficient inference (batching, caching, quantization).

Tier summary:
- Pay-as-you-go (Hosted): per-token pricing; volume discounts at 10M, 100M token bands.
- Predictable-Throughput (Dedicated): monthly reserved tokens/min + baseline compute fee; unlocked burst capacity billed at incremental rate. Includes SLA.
- Private (VPC/On-prem): annual license + optional support tier and observability add-ons.

Example pricing excerpt (illustrative numbers):
{
  "tier": "Predictable-Throughput",
  "reserved_tokens_min": "50k",
  "monthly_commit_usd": "22,000",
  "burst_price_per_1k_tokens_usd": "0.09",
  "observability_bundle": "included-30d"
}

Cost optimization levers we will promote:
- Enable prefix KV cache: reduces repeated token generation for templated prompts.
- Use quantized model variants for high-throughput, non-critical quality workloads.
- Configure batching policy to increase throughput for high concurrent traffic.

Roadmap & Themes (near-term: next 6 quarters)

Q4 2026 (current release window):
- v10 launch: unified API, policy engine GA, Predictable-Throughput pricing introduced, onboarding guide and cost estimator live.

Q1 2027:
- Runtime v3 alpha: kernel selection improvements and additional quantization profiles.
- SDK ergonomic improvements across Python/Go/Node.

Q2 2027:
- Enhanced private deployments: on-prem packaging automation and offline KMS certification.
- Expanded regional Dedicated capacity in APAC.

Q3 2027:
- Automatic workload tiering (ML-driven): move low-priority traffic to lower-cost variants automatically.
- Advanced analytics: per-prompt quality regression heatmaps in Console.

Rollout & release plan

1) Documentation & SDKs (T-4 weeks): publish migration guides, cost estimator, and SDK updates.
2) Internal canary (T-3 weeks): route 1% of internal traffic (redwood-internal routes) through policy engine + fallbacks, capture metrics.
3) External canary (T-2 weeks): invite 10 pilot customers to opt-in; monitor SLOs and quality guardrails.
4) Gradual rollout (T=0): 10%->50%->100% over 2 weeks with automated rollback on regression alerts.

Rollout monitoring checklist (examples):
- Latency p95 not exceeding threshold by >20% for >15m.
- Regression alerts fired for >2% of tracked prompt sets.
- Increase in 5xx errors over baseline >50%.

Migration & rollback steps (concise)

1) Prepare route config backups and export (console or CLI).
2) Enable policy engine in dry-run for route set A, inspect decisions and telemetry.
3) Flip to active with canary customers and monitor 24-72 hours.
4) If regression triggers: immediate rollback to previous route config, re-route to primary cluster, and open P1 in PagerDuty.

Release notes (v10 \u2014 2026-12-05)

Summary: v10 introduces the unified API and policy-driven routing with GA support for Predictable-Throughput pricing. Key customer-facing changes:
- Single API version (2026-12-v1) with streaming and resumable frames.
- Route-level policies and automatic cost-aware fallbacks.
- Predictable-Throughput Dedicated tier and updated Enterprise bundles.
- Improved batching and KV cache persistence for reduced unit costs.

Notable fixes and changes:
- Fixed: intermittent 503s when switching Dedicated pools during autoscale (SRE-4312).
- Added: route-level cache TTL configuration in Console and CLI.
- Changed: default streaming chunk size reduced to improve p95 for low-latency routes.

Open risks & mitigation

- Risk: Regression in user-perceived quality when fallback chooses quantized variants.
  - Mitigation: per-route quality thresholds + automatic rolling back of low-quality fallback variants; will run A/B evals for 30d during canary.
- Risk: Customers misconfigure latency thresholds, causing frequent fallbacks.
  - Mitigation: provide sane defaults, UI warnings, and a cost/latency estimator to preview behavior.

QA and launch checklist (must complete before GA)

- [ ] End-to-end tests across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with model variants
- [ ] Regression evals for top 50 customer prompt sets
- [ ] Load test achieving sustained batch sizes and target throughput
- [ ] Documentation and migration guides published
- [ ] Pricing page and cost estimator published
- [ ] Legal and finance sign-off on Predictable-Throughput contracts
